text:
Logan Wright: quick q for Suggestions beta — telemetry freshness. do we want to *block* showing savings estimates in Console if baseline cost metrics are older than N hours?

Logan Wright: context: we’re computing $/1M tokens baselines from token metering + route/model aggregates. sometimes pipelines lag (backfill, delayed partitions). UI currently just renders whatever `baseline_window_end` is.

Chloe Martin: +1, we’ve seen staging where baseline was like 36h behind and it looked “real” in the drawer. feels risky from a trust perspective.

Nadia Rahman: depends on what “block” means. if we block the whole suggestion, customers see empty state and assume product is broken. if we show but label “data stale”, that’s more honest.

Mei Lin: agree w/ Nadia. hard-blocking will nuke adoption metrics too. but we should not pretend it’s current.

Dylan Brooks: from Console side we can gate display on an API field. but we need a clear rule: hide savings numbers vs show with banner vs hide entire suggestion.

Jonas Weber: methodologically, stale baselines can skew savings quite a bit (esp. spiky workloads). but risk taxonomy already handles variance; freshness is orthogonal. I’d rather treat stale baseline as “insufficient data” for savings only.

Sana Farid: +1 — if `baseline_age_hours` is high, confidence interval is basically meaningless. we can still show recommendation rationale (why caching/batching helps) but savings should be suppressed or replaced w/ range like “—”.

Allison Grant: observability perspective: if the data is stale enough to suppress, that should page or at least alert. otherwise we’ll silently degrade the feature.

Logan Wright: proposal v0:
- if baseline age <= 6h: show savings normally
- 6h < age <= 24h: show savings + “Telemetry delayed” banner + include timestamp (“Based on data through …”) in basis section
- age > 24h: hide $ savings values (show “insufficient fresh telemetry”), but keep suggestion visible

Logan Wright: would also emit a metric `suggestions.baseline_stale_bucket` so we can track.

Chloe Martin: +1 on not hiding the whole suggestion. we can keep list row but savings column should show “—” and tooltip.

Dylan Brooks: UX: list has “Est. monthly impact”. if it’s “—” a lot, that’s going to look bad, but better than wrong numbers.

Nadia Rahman: 6h might be too aggressive. our token metering ETL is hourly but realistically can be ~2–3h behind depending on region. also private deployments can be slower.

Mei Lin: could make thresholds per deployment mode? Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Private in particular might have batch uploads.

Jonas Weber: careful: per-mode behavior makes docs harder. maybe keep global policy but allow backend to set `freshness_status` based on deployment.

Yara Haddad: backend can compute `freshness_status` = {fresh, delayed, stale} using tenant’s configured ingestion SLA. we already have per-tenant pipeline lag metrics.

Logan Wright: ok, so instead of hardcoding 6/24 in Console, Console uses `freshness_status` + `baseline_window_end` from suggestions-service.

Allison Grant: +1. and set alerting on % of tenants in stale status. otherwise we only hear via support.

Sana Farid: also: if we suppress savings, do we suppress confidence interval too? I think yes. don’t show CI if baseline is stale.

Chloe Martin: +1. drawer has “Estimated savings (p50 / p10–p90)”. If stale, replace with copy: “Savings estimate unavailable due to delayed telemetry.”

Dylan Brooks: does that conflict with ADR-0275 fields being “required”? UI can treat them as optional? we were trying to keep schema stable.

Logan Wright: ADR-0275 says required fields, but we can still return them and add a new top-level `savings_display_state` or `estimate_eligibility`. alternatively, keep numbers but add `is_stale=true` and UI chooses not to render. I prefer explicit state.

Jonas Weber: explicit state is better. reduces accidental rendering and overpromising.

Nadia Rahman: +1. if we keep sending numbers, someone will screenshot it and ignore the banner.

Mei Lin: action item: can we add `telemetry_freshness` object? (status + lag_hours + latest_partition_ts). but remember: no nested JSON in our doc generation :) (kidding)

Chloe Martin: lol. but yes, we can add fields flat:
- `baseline_window_end_ts`
- `baseline_lag_hours`
- `telemetry_freshness_status`
- `savings_rendering_policy` (show / show_with_warning / suppress)

Logan Wright: ok I’ll open a follow-up on ENG-2403 / ENG-2410 to add freshness fields + alert metric.

Allison Grant: pls loop SRE for the alert thresholds. I can help w/ dashboard panel: % suggestions returned with `telemetry_freshness_status=stale` by region.

Dylan Brooks: from Console: we’ll implement:
- list: savings cell shows “—” when `savings_rendering_policy=suppress`
- drawer: replaces savings section with “Telemetry delayed” callout and still shows rationale + assumptions

Jonas Weber: and docs should say: “Estimates use recent usage data; if telemetry is delayed, savings may not be shown.”

Logan Wright: :thumbsup: I’ll post draft thresholds once I look at pipeline lag distribution. I suspect 12h/48h might be more realistic than 6/24.

Nadia Rahman: please include private deployments in that analysis; they’ll skew.

Logan Wright: will do. closing loop here once I have numbers.
